beat: progression systems, trackable stats, missable content, RNG, difficulty, controls, version differences, multiplayer

findings.name: Item Percentage
findings.detail: The pause menu / Logbook shows an item-collection percentage. Counts include Energy Tanks, Missile Expansions, Shot (beam) Ammo Expansions, Psychic Power Bomb Expansions, and Mech Parts. Multiple sources indicate Power Suit items and Keys are weighted heavier than expansion-type pickups (a major upgrade can tick the percentage up by a full point, while several minor expansions might only add one point total), so the percentage is not a simple 1:1 count of collectibles.
findings.trackable: Displayed in the pause menu / Logbook screen; whether it also appears on a Samus Data-style file-select screen (as in past Prime titles) could not be confirmed — sources describe an in-menu tracker, not a file-select stat.

findings.name: Logbook Scan Percentage
findings.detail: Separate from item percentage: a Logbook/scan completion percentage tracks life forms and objects scanned via the Psychic Visor, across four categories (Biology, Machine, Lamorn Legacy, Technology).
findings.trackable: Logbook menu screen shows overall scan progress as a percentage.

findings.name: Green Energy Crystals
findings.detail: A separate crystal-collecting sidetrack with its own meter in the Mission menu (left side). Depositing crystals fills the meter; rewards unlock at 25/50/75/100%, granting permanent plasma cannon and control-beam upgrades plus a Green Energy Crystal radar finder. Once the meter reaches 100% (turns green->full), additional crystals continue filling a second, blue-colored pass of the same meter up to 200%; fully maxing (collecting every crystal in the game, filling the meter twice) unlocks bonus content in the in-game Gallery.
findings.trackable: Progress meter visible in the Mission menu.

findings.name: 100% completion secret ending
findings.detail: Reaching 100% item AND 100% scan completion unlocks an alternate version of the post-credits/ending scene (reportedly shown without Samus's helmet on) plus a secret post-credits scene with additional lore about the antagonist Sylux.
findings.trackable: Tied to the item and logbook percentage trackers reaching 100%.

findings.name: Missable Logbook scans (~10 total, contested exact list)
findings.detail: Unlike most mainline Prime backtracking design, a number of scans ARE permanently missable if not captured at specific story moments: three Prologue scans (enemies encountered before/at the Aberax fight, only chance since the Prologue area becomes inaccessible), several one-time boss/creature scans during unique encounters (e.g. a 'Swim Snatcher' creature that only appears once while grabbing an Energy Tank; a 'Behemoth' fight in Flare Pool; assorted boss projectile/phase scans). Sources disagree on the exact named list (one gives Space Pirate/GF Trooper/Aberax/Carvex Vine/Carvex Pollen Sac/Hover Shuttle Transport/Swim Snatcher/Behemoth/Lockjaw/Sylux = 10 scans; another gives a partly different list including Flight Drone MCU, Omega Griever, Varmis). Main story bosses (Carvex, Xelios, Keratos, Phenoros) CAN be rescanned later via a 'Playback Device'/psychic projector in the Sanctuary/Sanctum of the Guardians even if missed live in combat — this is described as a first for the series.
findings.trackable: Logbook screen shows which entries are filled/missing, but does not flag in advance which are about to become permanently missable.

findings.name: Point of no return — final area collectibles
findings.detail: Departing from prior Prime games' 'everything stays accessible via backtracking' convention: once the player triggers the endgame sequence at the top of Chrono Tower (an 'Order the Troopers to Move Forward' prompt leading into Sylux's final fight), all remaining Viewros areas become inaccessible and any uncollected Energy Tanks, Ammo Expansions, Scout Bots, and Mech Parts are permanently missed. A second, earlier point of no return exists on entering the Aberax boss arena in the Prologue (UTO Research Center), after which that area's other scans can no longer be obtained.
findings.trackable: Not flagged in-game beyond general story progression warnings (unconfirmed whether the game gives an explicit 'point of no return' warning prompt before locking players out).

findings.name: Scout Bots and Mech Parts
findings.detail: Two collectible categories distinct from standard ammo/energy expansions, scattered throughout Viewros and counted toward 100% completion. Exact total counts for Scout Bots, Mech Parts, Energy Tanks, Missile Expansions, Shot Expansions, and Power Bomb Expansions could not be confirmed via available sources.
findings.trackable: Presumed tracked via collection menu/map icons, unconfirmed exact display.

findings.name: Casual / Normal / Hard difficulty modes
findings.detail: Three difficulty settings: Casual (Samus has more HP, enemies die faster, energy/ammo refill on save), Normal (standard, no modifiers), and Hard (enemies take more hits and deal more damage; Save Stations only replenish Energy, not ammo). Casual and Normal are available from the start of a new game. Hard Mode unlocks only after completing the game once on Normal difficulty.
findings.trackable: Selected difficulty is presumably shown in pause/settings menu (unconfirmed if displayed on save file itself).

findings.name: Mid-game difficulty changes
findings.detail: Difficulty can be changed mid-playthrough via the Pause Menu settings, not just at new-game start. However, changing difficulty mid-game reportedly can forfeit some difficulty-based rewards/unlocks (exact rewards forfeited not specified in source).

findings.name: No New Game Plus
findings.detail: The game does not have a New Game Plus mode. Replaying a completed save (labeled 'Mission Complete') restarts progress from 0%.

findings.name: Gyro aiming
findings.detail: Gyro/motion aiming is supported on both Switch and Switch 2. Holding ZL and moving the right Joy-Con aims freely; locking onto an enemy shifts the Joy-Con into a gyro pointer mode similar to Metroid Prime Trilogy/Remastered. This is a standard, non-exclusive control option available on both platforms.

findings.name: Mouse Mode (Joy-Con 2) — Switch 2 exclusive
findings.detail: On Nintendo Switch 2 only, the right Joy-Con 2 can be placed flat (optical sensor/magnetic side down) to function as a mouse for aiming, offering higher precision. Switching between dual-stick, gyro/motion, and mouse control schemes happens contextually and seamlessly during play without needing to open a settings menu. This mouse control scheme does NOT exist on the original Nintendo Switch version — Joy-Con (1) lacks the necessary optical sensor for this mode.

findings.name: Single-player only
findings.detail: Metroid Prime 4: Beyond has no multiplayer or co-op mode of any kind; it is confirmed strictly single-player by both Retro Studios and Nintendo, unlike the multiplayer-inclusive spinoff Metroid Prime: Federation Force.

versionNotes.note: Switch 2: Quality Mode = dynamic/native up to 4K(2160p)/60fps docked, native 1080p/60fps handheld; Performance Mode = native 1080p/120fps docked, upscaled 1080p (from 720p)/120fps handheld. Both Switch 2 modes support HDR.
Switch 2 version has substantially faster load times than original Switch (~24s vs over a minute in one comparison video) and higher-resolution textures/shadows.

Mouse Mode aiming via Joy-Con 2 is exclusive to Nintendo Switch 2; not available/possible on original Switch hardware. Any trophy referencing mouse-mode play would be unverifiable/impossible on base Switch.
Could not confirm any GameChat-specific integration for this game on Switch 2.
Game is sold/listed both as a standard Switch version and a 'Nintendo Switch 2 Edition' / upgrade pack, per Nintendo's own store listings, confirming the two versions are distinct SKUs.
